video.title: This Might Be the Easiest Way to Sell AI to Businesses

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates a GoHighLevel AI agent that texts people after a local service business misses their call, answers questions and helps book an estimate. He shows how to tailor and duplicate the workflow, then prospect for customers using scraped business phone numbers and ringless voicemail. The video pitches a $500–$2,000 monthly service and shows a callback asking about price, but no sale is closed. Its core lesson is to automate the first response and lead qualification while giving the business owner a way to take over.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; demonstrates the workflow and describes the offer.

ideas.name: AI missed-call text-back service for local businesses
ideas.one_liner: Set up a tailored AI SMS agent that responds to missed calls, answers basic questions, qualifies leads and helps book estimates.
ideas.business_model: Recurring monthly service fee per client; the video also describes a 90-day money-back offer.
ideas.customer: Small service businesses that receive customer calls, such as tree-trimming companies, plumbers and HVAC businesses.
ideas.problem: Businesses miss calls and callers may not call back. A static text-back message does not answer follow-up questions or move the caller toward an appointment.
ideas.offer: Configure a GoHighLevel workflow that detects a missed call, sends a tailored SMS, has an AI agent ask about the customer’s need and details, and routes qualified, urgent or unqualified contacts appropriately. The owner or an employee can take over the conversation.

pricing.model: Monthly fee per client; a 90-day payback guarantee is presented in the sales agent’s response.

price_points.label: Price stated in the sales conversation

pricing.notes: No setup fee is stated. The host says the service is offered with a refund if it does not pay for itself within 90 days. The demonstrated prospect asks about price, but the host says no sale has closed.

acquisition_channels.details: The host exports local business phone numbers from Outscraper, uploads them to a ringless voicemail service, and leaves a broad message asking the business to call back. The callback triggers the missed-call text-back workflow; the AI answers questions and flags hot leads for a human follow-up. The transcript does not establish that this outreach method is compliant for UK use.

quote.text: I went to outscraper.com. I typed in treeming businesses in Dallas, Texas. It gave me this info. And all I care about is the phone number.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The provider configures a GoHighLevel workflow and adapts its prompts and branches to the client’s trade. After setup, the software sends SMS messages, handles routine conversation, records lead details and sends owner notifications. The business owner or employee handles handoffs and carries out estimates and physical service work.
unit_economics_claims: The host states a target price range of $500–$2,000 per client per month.
The sales conversation states a $500 monthly price with a refund if the service does not pay for itself within 90 days.
The host reports no money received from the demonstrated prospecting test so far; the callback is not a closed sale.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated. The host mentions a GoHighLevel free trial; paid platform, phone and ringless-voicemail costs are not stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. The demo generates a callback and price question, but no sale is closed.

acquisition.how: The demonstrated campaign uses software to send ringless voicemails, but a person selects and cleans the list, creates the recording and campaign, and closes interested leads. The UK legality and suitability of this outbound method are not established in the video.

onboarding.how: A human must gather the client’s services, coverage area, questions, phone setup and handoff rules, then adapt and verify the prompt and workflow. The workflow can be duplicated to reduce repeated setup.

delivery.how: Once configured, the agent can handle routine SMS conversations and qualify leads without the owner in each exchange. It sends notifications and supports a human takeover; the client still performs estimates and physical work.

billing.how: The video states monthly pricing but does not show invoicing, payment collection or subscription management.

support.how: The agent answers routine questions, but the owner or employee needs to handle emergencies, qualified leads and cases the bot cannot resolve. Ongoing client support is not described.

uk_applicability.notes: The missed-call response and appointment-qualification service can suit UK trades, but the video’s acquisition tactic uses ringless voicemail to numbers gathered from a business list, with no compliance discussion. UK marketing SMS to individuals and sole traders requires prior consent; cold-call follow-ups must be screened against TPS/CTPS. A UK version should use compliant acquisition and SMS practices, local service details and locally appropriate pricing.

risks: The host says no client sale has been closed in the demonstration, so the price and acquisition method are not validated by a completed sale.

The demo’s scraped-list ringless voicemail outreach and follow-up need compliance review before use in the UK. Marketing SMS to individuals and sole traders requires prior consent, and cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.
The AI could misunderstand a service request or give an unsuitable answer; the workflow needs accurate client information and a reliable human handoff.
Urgent property or safety situations need prompt human attention; a bot notification is not a substitute for the service business’s response.
The 90-day refund offer could create losses if the client’s return cannot be measured or the service does not generate enough business.
GoHighLevel, telephony and ringless-voicemail costs are not stated, so margins cannot be assessed from the transcript.

tactics.name: Build the missed-call workflow from a template
steps: In GoHighLevel, start from the missed-call text template and use busy, voicemail or no-answer calls as triggers.
Add a short delay before texting, assign an owner or employee, tag the contact and configure notifications.
Replace the static text with Conversation AI and tailor its personality, objectives, questions and examples to the client’s trade.
Set a reply-wait period and a response cap, then add branches for booked estimates, emergencies and unqualified contacts.
Publish the workflow and test the handoff and notification behavior.

quote.text: This is the most important part. Remember this step right here where you first send the text to the customer? We're going to delete that.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Tailor the agent to one trade
steps: Use a specific business name, service area and appointment goal in the prompt.
Have the agent ask what service the caller needs and gather the details needed for an estimate.
Use an LLM to draft or trim the instructions and example responses to fit the platform’s stated word limits.
Add separate handling for urgent cases and requests outside the service area.

quote.text: So, you don't have to like upload this huge repository of FAQs, just have AI create that knowledge base for you.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Duplicate the workflow for each client and for prospecting
steps: Duplicate the configured client workflow rather than rebuilding it for every business.
Swap the trade-specific details and prompt for each new client.
For prospecting, duplicate the workflow again, change the agent to answer as the seller and qualify interested business owners, and remove irrelevant emergency handling.
Flag hot leads with their name and phone number so a person can follow up.

quote.text: Now that you have this one workflow, you can copy and paste it over and over and over for multiple customers.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Dogfood the text-back agent to get prospects
steps: Use a business directory scraper to collect local businesses in the chosen trade and area.
Normalize the phone numbers and export the list as a CSV.
Record a short, broad voicemail asking business owners to call back, then upload it and the list to a ringless-voicemail service.
Sync the caller ID with GoHighLevel so returned calls can trigger the prospecting workflow.
Let the AI handle basic questions and pricing, then personally call or meet qualified leads to close.

quote.text: Hey, this is Chris Kerner. I'm here in Dallas, Texas, and I'm looking for a tree trimming business. So please give me a call back. Thanks.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Offer a measurable payback guarantee
steps: State a monthly price clearly when a prospect asks.
Tie the refund promise to whether the service pays for itself within the stated period.
Track client outcomes carefully before relying on the guarantee as a repeatable sales offer.

quote.text: Great question. It is $500 a month, but if it doesn't pay for itself in the first 90 days, then I'll give you all your money back.

warnings.warning: The outbound prospecting method uses ringless voicemail to a list of scraped business numbers. The transcript does not address UK compliance. Marketing SMS to individuals and sole traders requires prior consent, and cold-call follow-ups must be screened against TPS/CTPS.

lessons.lesson: Responding quickly matters in a missed-call funnel, but the video’s 57% figure is cited as data without a source in the transcript.

quote.text: 57% of sales goes to whoever responds first. And that's not my opinion. That's data.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A single acknowledgement may not resolve a caller’s questions; a two-way conversation can gather the details needed to move toward an appointment.

quote.text: there's no interaction, there's no engagement. That doesn't really do a lot at all. But we're going to add AI to it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Make the agent specific to the customer’s trade, services and service area instead of relying on a generic prompt.

quote.text: I'm going to market this to tree trimming business owners cuz I own a tree trimming business. So I know that industry better than most.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Build guardrails and escalation paths into the workflow: cap responses, distinguish emergencies and notify a person when a lead is ready.

quote.text: What's the max number of responses that we want the bot to give? This is like an insurance policy, a safeguard against the bot just going crazy and not leaving the person alone.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Reuse a working workflow across similar clients, changing the trade-specific prompt and information for each business.

quote.text: Now that you have this one workflow, you can copy and paste it over and over and over for multiple customers.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use the service’s own acquisition method to test it on prospects, but distinguish a callback or price question from a closed sale.

quote.text: So, I haven't closed them yet. I don't have money in my pocket yet from this, but you can see that this works.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A payback guarantee can make an offer easier to understand, but the seller needs a way to measure whether the service paid for itself.

quote.text: Great question. It is $500 a month, but if it doesn't pay for itself in the first 90 days, then I'll give you all your money back.
quote.speaker: AI agent (on-screen text scripted by Chris Koerner)

evidence_quality.rationale: The host demonstrates a detailed workflow and an outbound test, but no customer sale or client result is shown. The response-speed statistic is not sourced in the transcript, and the pricing and guarantee are presented as an offer rather than established unit economics.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host identifies GoHighLevel as a channel supporter, offers an affiliate link and says a paid signup supports his channel. He also promotes his Playmakers community.
